- **Novel mode (full-screen text)** (Input: What to do?): Switches to "novel mode": the text fills the whole screen over a darkened background and the lines of “Say a line” pile up one under the other, like in a book. When the page is full, it turns by itself. "New page" clears it right away; "Back to the dialogue box" brings back the usual box. Example: A night-time narration in novel mode, then back to the dialogue box for the conversation.
- **SMS mode (phone conversation)** (Inputs: What to do?, Who writes to you (name and photo on top), Who is "me" (their lines on the right), Text under the name (empty = "online")): Shows the conversation as text messages on a phone: the lines of “Say a line” become bubbles (on the left for whoever writes, with three little dots "…" before they appear) and the answers of “Ask a choice” are picked at the bottom of the phone, then arrive on the right. The narrator writes a small caption in the middle (for example "Last night, 10:14 pm"). "Who writes to you" gives the name and photo at the top; "Who is me" makes a character write on the right without going through a choice. "Clear the conversation" empties the phone; "Back to the dialogue box" leaves the mode. Everything is set in the Dialogue style: colours, size, time of the "…", full-screen phone… Example: SMS mode (turn on, who writes to you: Hana) → Say a line (Hana: "Are you there?") → Ask a choice ("Yes, tell me" / "Why?").
- **Unlock an achievement** (Inputs: Achievement name, Description (shown in the list), Achievement image (empty = a star), Hint while it is hidden (empty = none)): Unlocks an achievement: an "Achievement unlocked!" banner slides in at the top of the screen (only the first time in the published game; every time in the editor so you can see it). The achievement joins the "Achievements" tab of "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen”: it stays hidden behind "???" (with a hint if you write one) until it is won. Put one at the end of a story, in a secret branch, after “Friendship (hearts)”… The banner is set in the Dialogue style: colours, frame image, time, place (top or bottom), sound. Example: End the story (ending "The lost sock") → Unlock an achievement (name "The lost sock", description "Secret ending found").
- **Replayable scene (gallery)** (Inputs: Start or end of the scene, Scene name (gallery)): Marks a scene the player can watch again from "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen” ("Scenes to replay" tab). Put one at the "Start of the scene": when the story passes it, the scene unlocks and the state of the story is remembered. Put another at the "End of the scene": when replaying, the story stops there and goes back to the gallery. Nothing is saved during a replay. Music started with “Play music” also unlocks in the "Music" tab. Example: "The clearing": one node at the start of the meeting with Hana, another right after she leaves.
- **End the story** (Input: Ending name (optional: it counts in "Endings and gallery")): Clears the dialogue box, the characters and the background of the story: the game takes over again. If you give an "Ending name", this ending is remembered forever and counts in "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen”; the saved game is erased. Example: "Friends of the cabin" after the last line, then back to the title screen.
- **Friendship (hearts)** (Inputs: Who?, Hearts to add (−1 to remove), Maximum number of hearts): Adds (or removes, with −1) friendship hearts for a character, up to the maximum. The hearts show at the top left during the story and a “+1 ❤” floats up (they can be hidden in the Dialogue style). They are saved with the game and restored by ◀ Back. Example: after the kind answer “I'll stay with you”: Hana +1.
- **If the friendship…** (Inputs: Who?, is, hearts  →  Outputs: True / False): Picks how the story goes on from a character's friendship hearts: the “True” output if the comparison is true, otherwise “False”. For an ending that depends on how you treated the characters. Example: if Hana's friendship is at least 4 → the happy ending, otherwise the sad one.
- **Story title screen** (Inputs: Story title, Background picture (empty = the current background)  →  Output: New game): Shows the story title over a picture, with big buttons: "Continue" (resumes where the player left off, with the background, characters, music and variables: the story saves itself at every line), "New game" (the output: the start of the story) and "Endings and gallery" (endings found and backgrounds already seen, the others are locked). During the story, the ◀ Back button returns to the previous line, even before a choice. Example: placed right after "At start"; every “End the story” comes back to it.
- **Ask the player for a text (name…)** (Inputs: Variable, Question, Suggested answer): Opens a small window with the keyboard: the player types a text (their name…), stored in the chosen variable; it continues when they tap OK. In lines, {prenom} shows this text. Example: "What's your name?" → variable prenom → “Say a line” "Nice to meet you, {prenom}!".

### Screen filters

- **Screen filter** (Inputs: Filter, Strength (%), Fade in (seconds), Duration (seconds, 0 = endless), Keep in the next scene, Also filter buttons and texts (HUD), Flashlight: lit object (name; empty = the one the camera follows), Flashlight: light size (%)  →  Outputs: Then / When it's over): Gives the whole game a “look”, buttons and texts included: TV, VHS, black and white, underwater, nightmare, flashlight… 32 filters to choose from. It fades in gently, stays as long as you want (0 = until you stop it) and can carry on into the next scene. “Then” runs right away, “When it's over” at the end of the duration. Example: the hero is hit: “Hurt” filter for 2 seconds; or “Flashlight” in a cave.
- **Stop the filter** (Input: Fade out (seconds)  →  Outputs: Then / When it's over): Gently fades out the current screen filter. “Then” runs right away, “When it's over” once the filter is gone. Example: the hero leaves the cave: stop the flashlight in 1 second.

### Physics

- **Set the physics world** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Gravity downwards (%, 100 = normal, 0 = space, negative = upwards), Gravity to the right (%, negative = left: a constant wind), Precision, Resting objects fall asleep (lighter on the phone)): Sets the physics world of the scene: gravity downwards (100% = normal, 0 = space, negative = objects fall upwards), sideways gravity (a wind that always blows), calculation precision and whether resting objects fall asleep. Use it once, under “At start”. It only affects objects that have the “Realistic physics” behavior (⚙ Behavior). Example: a level on the Moon: gravity 20%.
- **Adjust a physics object** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Object type, Material (weight, bounce and grip at once), Contact shape, Weight (%, 100 = normal, empty = unchanged), Bounce (0 to 100, empty = unchanged), Grip (0 = ice, 100 = sticky, empty = unchanged), Object gravity (%, 0 = floats, empty = unchanged), Air drag (0 to 20, empty = unchanged), Top speed (pixels per second, 0 = no limit, empty = unchanged), Never rotates, Ghost (things pass through), Very fast object (never goes through a thin wall), Object layer (1 to 8, empty = unchanged)): Changes the settings of a physics object during the game: its type (normal, fixed, guided, or no more physics), material (wood, stone, metal, rubber, ball, ice, feather), shape, weight, bounce, grip, gravity, air drag, top speed, whether it rotates, whether it is a ghost or very fast, its layer. Any setting left empty or on “(do not change)” stays as it is. On an object without physics yet, choosing a type gives it physics. Example: a ball that turns into rubber (material “Rubber”) when a bonus is picked up.
- **Push (physics force)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Push to the right (negative = to the left), Push downwards (negative = upwards), How, Where to push (off-center, the object starts to spin), Does weight matter?): Pushes a physics object with a force. “Steady push”: repeat it every frame (under “Every frame” or “Finger down”), the object speeds up as long as you push (a rocket, a wind, a fan). “A hit”: adds speed at once (a jump, a kick). By default the effect is the same on a light or heavy object; in the advanced settings you can make weight matter, and push away from the center to make the object spin. Values: pixels per second (per second squared for the steady push). Example: a rocket game: “Finger down” → push upwards (-2500) steadily.
- **Set the speed (physics)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Speed to the right (pixels per second, empty = unchanged), Speed downwards (negative = upwards, empty = unchanged), Spin speed (degrees per second, empty = unchanged), How, Stop everything at once?): Sets the speed of a physics object, in pixels per second: to the right, downwards (negative = upwards) and spin in degrees per second. Any box left empty leaves that speed unchanged. “Replace” gives exactly this speed; “Add” adds it to the current speed. The “Stop everything” option sets all speeds to zero. Perfect for a jump (downward speed of -900), a sharp stop or a character moving at constant speed. Example: a platformer jump: downward speed = -900, only if “If the physics object…” says the object is standing on something.
- **Launch (angle and speed)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Angle (degrees: 0 = right, -90 = up, 90 = down, 180 = left), Starting speed (pixels per second), How): Launches a physics object in a direction: you give the angle (0 = to the right, -90 = up, 90 = down, 180 = to the left) and the starting speed. Gravity then does the rest: the object follows a curve. Ideal for a slingshot game, a cannon, a ball throw. The angle can be a formula (for example the angle between the object and the finger). Example: a slingshot: when the finger lets go, launch the bird at the angle of the elastic.
- **Explosion (physics blast)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Center: X position (empty = at the object's center), Center: Y position (empty = at the object's center), Blast radius (pixels), Force at the center (speed given, pixels per second), Only objects with this tag (empty = all)): Blasts every physics object around a point: the closer to the center, the harder they are thrown, and they start to spin. The center is the middle of the chosen object, or an (x, y) point if you write one. You set the blast radius and the force (the speed given at the center). Option: only objects with a certain tag. The node destroys nothing: combine it with “Particle effect” and “Destroy object” for a real explosion. Example: a bomb: when it touches the ground, explosion with radius 500 and force 1800, then destroy the bomb.
- **Link two objects** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Kind of link, Link name (to adjust or cut it later), Point of object A where the link is made, Point of object B (rod, spring, rope), Shift the point to the right (pixels), Shift the point downwards (pixels), Do the two objects collide?, Length (pixels, 0 = the starting distance), Spring or suspension stiffness (1 = soft, 10 = firm), Damping (0 to 100: higher means less bouncing), Lower limit (degrees for a hinge, pixels for a slider; empty = none), Upper limit (degrees or pixels; empty = none), Rail or suspension direction (degrees: 0 = horizontal, 90 = vertical; empty = automatic), Motor: speed (degrees per second for a hinge or wheel, pixels per second for a slider; 0 = no motor), Motor or brake strength (1 = weak, 10 = normal, 100 = very strong)): Links two objects so they hold or move together, like in real life. Kind of link: hinge (swings around a point: door, pendulum), rigid rod (fixed distance), spring (elastic, with stiffness), rope (maximum length), slider (slides along a rail, with limits and motor), weld (stuck together), wheel with suspension (car: A = the body, B = the wheel, with motor), brake (top view). Object B is optional: without B, object A is attached to a fixed point of the scenery. Give the link a name to adjust it (“Adjust a link”) or cut it (“Cut a link”) later. In the advanced settings: point on each side, limits, rail direction, motor, collision between the two objects. Both objects need the “Realistic physics” behavior (except a fixed support). Example: a pendulum: A = the ball, B = a small fixed object at the top, type “Hinge” or “Rigid rod”; a bridge: planks linked by hinges.
- **Adjust a link** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Link name, Motor: speed (0 = stop the motor, empty = unchanged), Motor strength (empty = unchanged), Spring or suspension stiffness (empty = unchanged), New length (pixels, empty = unchanged), New lower limit (empty = unchanged), New upper limit (empty = unchanged), Limits): Changes a link already created by “Link two objects” (found by its name): start, stop or speed up its motor, set its strength, the stiffness of a spring or suspension, the length of a rod or rope, the limits. Any empty box stays as before. Example: a car whose wheel motor starts when a button is pressed. Example: “Gas” button: adjust the link “rear_wheel” with motor = 720; on release: motor = 0.
- **Cut a link** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Name of the link to cut, Or: name of an object whose links are all cut): Cuts a link: write its name, or write an object's name to cut all of its links. The objects separate and each falls on its own (a collapsing bridge, a cut rope, a detaching cabin). Example: a trapped bridge: when the hero touches the lever, cut the link “plank_3”.
- **Grab with the finger (physics)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Action, Only objects with this tag (empty = all), Softness of the grip): Lets you grab a physics object with the finger and drag it, like in real life: the object follows the finger with a bit of elasticity, pushes the others and can get stuck. Put it under “Finger down” (action “Grab and drag”): while the finger is down, the object under it is dragged; as soon as the finger lifts, it is released by itself (or use the “Let go” action). You can restrict the grab to objects with a tag, and set the softness of the grip. Example: a crate puzzle: the player moves crates with a fingertip to build a tower.
- **If the physics object…** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Question, Speed from which it counts (pixels per second), Grace time (seconds, for “has just touched the ground”)  →  Outputs: True / False): Asks a question about a physics object and follows the “true” or “false” exit: is it standing on something (to allow a jump), does it touch something, does it touch something above, is it at rest (asleep), is it moving fast, falling, rising. For “moves fast”, “falling” and “rising” the threshold in pixels per second is set in the advanced settings. You can also read values directly in a formula: object.vitesse, object.masse, object.vitesseRotation. Example: a platformer jump: “Jump button” → If the object is standing on something → set downward speed to -900.
